land.text: the Bahamas: 'Britain made the Bahamas a crown colony in 1718'; internal autonomy from 7 January 1964; independence 10 July 1973

predecessors.note: The colony was taken by Spain in 1782 and exchanged back under the 1783 preliminaries; declared a British colony again in 1784 (The Bahamas page).

capitals.name: Nassau
capitals.note: 'Nassau, the capital city of the Bahamas, lies on the island of New Providence.'

correction.text: the archipelago of 'some 700 islands and 2,400 cays': the Cliopatria polygon plus the whole country, so that cays the polygon misses are not dropped

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 18,694 km2 against the infobox 13,880 km2 (land 10,010 km2) is a ratio of 1.35, within a factor of two. The polygon covers 49 of the 58 grid cells of Natural Earth's Bahamas (14 cells of the country, mostly the north-eastern and central cays, are missing and 5 cells lie outside it), so the union is a gap-filler, not a change of extent.

region.text: the Bahamas, 'some 700 islands and 2,400 cays in total', capital Nassau on New Providence

ledger.note: 10 July 1973: the Bahamas becomes independent. 'The Order came into force on 10 July 1973' (the independence order, dated 20 June 1973); the country 'joined the Commonwealth of Nations on the same day'. Officially the Commonwealth of The Bahamas.

certainty.note: Island coasts; the page gives no maritime or land boundary dispute, and describes the Turks and Caicos only as the neighbouring British territory of the Lucayan archipelago.

sources.title: The Bahamas
sources.note: Identity, infobox area 13,880 km2, Nassau, 1964 internal autonomy, 10 July 1973 independence, crown colony 1718, Spanish capture 1782.

notes: One page opened (budget 1-2); the shape never changes and the page names no dispute or transfer. Internal autonomy (7 January 1964) is not modelled as a vassal period because Cliopatria begins the state in 1973 and the state's own record before independence is that of a colony. Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape (1969-1995) still contains the Bahamas (44 of the country's 58 cells, checked with the gazetteer for 1966-1995), so the British Colonial Empire dossier (eu-11) must release the Bahamas in 1973. Cell check: the Cliopatria polygon resolves to 49 cells against 58 for Natural Earth's Bahamas, hence the union gap-filler.
